notes:
TBox rule edit. No real exceptions: the HTML standard lists the void elements (area, base, br, col, embed, hr, img, input, link, meta, source, track, wbr) and forbids an end tag on every one; the self-closing slash is not an end tag, and SVG/MathML elements are foreign, not void. The counterfactual (void elements must be closed, as in XHTML-style markup) is plausible and clearly false. is the well-known member: its missing closing tag is taught by name. In w1 it leaves the void class but keeps taking no content, so nothing outside the chain breaks (the other void elements keep their own status). and are invented, so the rule is their only route. The near query (the hyperlink element, ) differs from the new answer (yes) and does not follow from the edit; one that asked whether a void element may hold content was avoided, since the edit could plausibly be read as changing it. Scope: the rule is the HTML syntax's (the WHATWG syntax section says it 'only describes the rules for resources labeled with an HTML MIME type'); in the XML syntax (XHTML)

is well-formed, which is why the prompts say 'in HTML'. The end-tag rule is exact in the standard: 'end tags must not be specified for void elements'; the parser's handling of a stray
as
is error recovery, not a valid end tag.
